concepts.name: Concurrency versus parallelism
concepts.summary: Explain that concurrency is structuring work as overlapping tasks while parallelism is literally executing tasks at the same instant on multiple cores.

concepts.name: Threads and processes
concepts.summary: Describe a process as an isolated program instance with its own memory and a thread as an execution path sharing its process's memory.

concepts.name: Shared mutable state
concepts.summary: Recognise that data accessible and modifiable by several threads is the root of most concurrency bugs.

concepts.name: Nondeterministic interleaving
concepts.summary: Understand that the scheduler may interleave instructions of different threads in varying orders, so results can differ between runs.

concepts.name: Race condition
concepts.summary: Explain that a race condition occurs when the outcome depends on the timing of unsynchronised accesses to shared data.

concepts.name: Starting and joining threads
concepts.summary: Recall that threads are started to run a function and joined to wait for their completion.

misconceptions.text: Concurrent programs always run faster than sequential ones.
If a program gave the right answer once, it has no race condition.
Threads in the same program each have their own separate copy of all variables.

concepts.name: Critical sections and mutual exclusion
concepts.summary: Identify code that touches shared data and protect it so only one thread executes it at a time.

concepts.name: Locks and mutexes
concepts.summary: Use a lock to guard shared data, acquiring before access and always releasing afterwards, including on error paths.

concepts.name: Atomic operations
concepts.summary: Understand that an atomic operation completes indivisibly and why a plain increment is not atomic.

concepts.name: Deadlock
concepts.summary: Describe how threads each holding a lock the other needs wait forever.

concepts.name: Thread-safe code
concepts.summary: Judge and make simple functions and data structures safe to call from multiple threads.

concepts.name: Thread pools and tasks
concepts.summary: Submit units of work to a fixed pool of workers instead of creating a thread per task.

concepts.name: Producer-consumer queues
concepts.summary: Pass work between threads through a thread-safe queue rather than sharing raw variables.

misconceptions.text: Locking every method of a class automatically makes any use of it correct.
A single statement like counter++ is atomic.
Deadlock only happens when many threads are involved.

concepts.name: Coffman deadlock conditions
concepts.summary: Analyse a deadlock by identifying mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait.

concepts.name: Lock ordering and avoidance
concepts.summary: Prevent deadlocks by imposing a global lock order, shrinking lock scope or using try-lock with timeouts.

concepts.name: Condition variables and signalling
concepts.summary: Coordinate threads waiting for a state change using condition variables, rechecking predicates in a loop.

concepts.name: Semaphores and barriers
concepts.summary: Choose semaphores, latches or barriers to limit access or synchronise phases of work.

concepts.name: Memory visibility and ordering
concepts.summary: Analyse why one thread may not see another's writes without synchronisation and how happens-before guarantees fix this.

concepts.name: Starvation and livelock
concepts.summary: Distinguish deadlock from starvation and livelock and diagnose each from symptoms.

concepts.name: Immutability and confinement
concepts.summary: Avoid locking by sharing only immutable data or keeping mutable data owned by one thread.

concepts.name: Futures and async results
concepts.summary: Represent a pending result with a future and compose or await it without blocking unnecessarily.

misconceptions.text: A condition variable wait can use an if check because wakeups always mean the condition holds.
Without a lock, a write by one thread becomes visible to others immediately.
Using volatile or similar flags makes compound operations thread-safe.

concepts.name: Actor and message-passing models
concepts.summary: Evaluate message passing with actors or channels against shared-memory locking for a given problem.

concepts.name: Lock-free and wait-free techniques
concepts.summary: Analyse compare-and-swap based structures, including the ABA problem and the trade-offs against locks.

concepts.name: Lock contention and granularity
concepts.summary: Evaluate coarse, fine-grained and read-write locking choices by their contention and complexity costs.

concepts.name: Scalability limits
concepts.summary: Use Amdahl's law and overhead analysis to judge how much parallelism will actually speed a workload.

concepts.name: CPU-bound versus I/O-bound workloads
concepts.summary: Classify workloads and match them to threads, processes or async I/O accordingly.

concepts.name: Event loops and async/await
concepts.summary: Analyse how an event loop interleaves non-blocking tasks on one thread and where blocking calls stall it.

concepts.name: Backpressure and cancellation
concepts.summary: Design pipelines that bound queues, propagate cancellation and clean up resources when tasks fail.

concepts.name: Cache effects and false sharing
concepts.summary: Analyse how cache-line sharing between cores degrades parallel performance.

misconceptions.text: Async/await code runs in parallel on multiple cores by default.
Lock-free algorithms are always faster than lock-based ones.
Adding more threads always improves throughput until cores run out.

concepts.name: Formal concurrency correctness
concepts.summary: Evaluate designs against safety and liveness properties and linearizability using invariants and formal reasoning.

concepts.name: Hardware memory models
concepts.summary: Judge when acquire-release or relaxed atomics are valid given language and hardware reordering rules.

concepts.name: Concurrent data structure design
concepts.summary: Create concurrent data structures balancing correctness, progress guarantees and scalability, including safe memory reclamation.

concepts.name: Systematic concurrency testing
concepts.summary: Evaluate and apply race detectors, stress tests, deterministic schedulers and model checking to find rare interleavings.

concepts.name: Concurrency architecture selection
concepts.summary: Design a system-level concurrency architecture combining threads, async, actors and processes to meet latency and throughput goals.

concepts.name: Distributed concurrency hazards
concepts.summary: Assess how partial failure, unreliable clocks and message reordering change local concurrency assumptions across machines.

concepts.name: Production concurrency diagnosis
concepts.summary: Diagnose live hangs, tail latency and contention using thread dumps, profilers and tracing, and judge the fix.

misconceptions.text: Passing a large number of stress-test runs proves a concurrent program is correct.
On modern hardware, sequential consistency can be assumed for ordinary memory accesses.
Distributed locks behave like local mutexes and give the same guarantees.
